blocks.text:
An early departure is planned at around 6:00–7:00 a.m. Follow the Liana Chica trail to Sacha's suspended canopy walkway, about 3 km from the Napo River and 1.5 km from the lodge.

The walkway rises 36 metres above the forest and extends for about 275 metres. Two of the three towers have intermediate platforms every 12 metres, allowing you to climb in stages. From above, you can explore the rainforest canopy, where birds that are almost impossible to spot from the ground come into view.

After the canopy walk, continue along the Liana Grande trail through the low-lying igapó floodplain. Local guides explain how plants have been used for centuries in everyday life and traditional medicine. Species that may look alike to a first-time Amazon visitor become easier to distinguish. Next, the Higuerón trail winds through old-growth forest beneath enormous kapok and fig trees rising tens of metres into the air.

After lunch, choose between a relaxed walk along the Napo River and the more active Leoncillo trail, where you may spot dusky titi monkeys. Both walks end at a wooden landing, where you board a canoe back to the lodge.

Meals: breakfast, lunch and dinner.

blocks.text:
After breakfast, begin a walk along the Lagartococha trail. Your guide will discuss the lives of local Indigenous communities, their relationship with the forest and traditional beliefs. According to local traditions, ancestral spirits inhabit certain trees, while a forest spirit known as the dwende roams the woodland.

At Lake Lagartococha, board a canoe to explore natural wetlands where anacondas, caimans and capybaras may be seen. On the walking section beside the lake, look out for capuchin and squirrel monkeys.

Return to the lodge to rest, swim or relax in a hammock. After lunch, a local guide demonstrates traditional piranha-fishing techniques.

At around 3:30 p.m., set out on a quiet canoe ride through the flooded forest. Squirrel monkeys, capuchins and howler monkeys inhabit the treetops; with luck, you may also see river otters or three-toed sloths. The boat moves slowly and almost silently, making this an excellent wildlife-watching route. Continue to a wooden observation tower built around an ancient kapok tree. The approved 2027 programme describes it as 41 metres high. Use telescopes to watch birds, and on a clear day enjoy distant views of Mount Sumaco and the snow-covered Andes. As the sun sets, the rainforest canopy gradually darkens.

The return journey takes place after sunset. At night, the forest sounds completely different: frogs, insects and nocturnal birds call, bats fly over the water, and caimans may appear in the channels.

Meals: breakfast, lunch and dinner.
